recognize_zh: 低倍即可見大量紅血球內含纖細的環狀體（ring form），部分有雙染色質點、部分紅血球同時被多隻寄生蟲感染，受感染紅血球大小正常，且不見滋養體或裂殖體，符合惡性瘧（Plasmodium falciparum）。
features: High parasitemia with numerous red cells containing small delicate ring forms
Rings with double chromatin dots and appliqué (accolé) forms at the red cell margin
Infected red cells are not enlarged and lack Schüffner stippling
Absence of mature trophozoites and schizonts in the peripheral blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low-to-intermediate power shows a high parasite burden, with numerous red cells containing small, delicate ring-form trophozoites. Double chromatin dots, appliqué forms at the red cell periphery, and red cells infected by more than one parasite are readily identified. Infected red cells are normal in size without stippling, and no mature trophozoites, schizonts, or banana-shaped gametocytes are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium falciparum malaria; percent parasitemia should be quantified.

ddx.vs: Babesia rings are pleomorphic, may form tetrad (Maltese cross) arrangements, lack hemozoin pigment, and are not accompanied by gametocytes.
Infected red cells are enlarged with Schüffner stippling, and all stages including ameboid trophozoites and schizonts are seen.
Early rings can mimic falciparum but band-form trophozoites and schizonts appear in blood; PCR is needed for species confirmation.
Superimposed platelets lack a cytoplasmic ring with a discrete chromatin dot and lie in a different focal plane.
